set.descent_text: Finish the dihedral and the short ledges to the large bench above the roof. A fixed pin and nut there serve as the rappel anchor back to the start of the route.
set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. Bullett is on the low feature directly beneath and left of Hallett Chimney, in front of the north face, and climbs the big dihedral under a roof. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for position, bench and rappel anchor; area and Tyndall Gully pages for the trail.

set.descent_text: The variation rejoins Bullett just below its anchor, so descend as for Bullett: rappel from the anchor on the bench above, back to the start.
set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. The line climbs the left wall of the Bullett dihedral, so use the Bullett start under the north face. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Dodging the Bullet page says it climbs the first pitch of Bullett then rejoins before the anchor; Bullett page gives the rappel.

set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. Ms. Inferno is a short route about 100 feet left of Bullett, near the left-hand arete, where a crack system begins well above the ground. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for position relative to Bullett; descent not stated, omitted.

set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. Booby Trap climbs the indistinct, ledgy buttress between The Cleft and Hallett Couloir. The line begins at the base of the rock buttress, immediately right of where The Cleft's couloir starts. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for position; The Cleft page places it 100 feet east of Hallett Couloir; top-out not clear, so no descent.

set.descent_text: The route finishes at the blocky summit. Descend Hallett Couloir, or if snow conditions in that couloir are dangerous, walk off the back of the peak and down toward Lake Haiyaha, then follow the trail from there back to Dream Lake.
set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. The Cleft begins on the north side of the east ridge, about 100 feet east of Hallett Couloir. Ascend a steep, narrow couloir for a few hundred feet, then turn right on low fifth-class ground toward the cleft in the cliffs above. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; Booby Trap page agrees on its position relative to Hallett Couloir.

set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. Aim for the western edge of the Third Buttress, which forms the right skyline of the north face. The route starts near that edge, below the tall, vertical V-groove of the second pitch. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for the start; top-out not clear so descent omitted.

set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. The Slit is the obvious gash between the Second and Third Buttresses. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; top-out not stated so descent omitted.

set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. Hallett Chimney splits the north side of the peak, separating the First Buttress from the Second. The chimney funnels falling rock and ice, so do not linger below parties above. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; Englishman's Route page also places the chimney on the north face; top-out not stated so descent omitted.

set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. The route starts up the prominent dihedral of the First Buttress. Snow slopes at its base can be prone to avalanche. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for position; the exit is on the summit ridge but no descent is given, so omitted.

set.descent_text: The route ends at the top of the Second Buttress. From there, follow the ridge east until a bolted anchor marks the first rappel. Two rappels are usual, with a two-rope or 70 m rope set-up making the first easy; then follow a cairned third and fourth class line back through gullies and trees to the base of the first buttress.
set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the trail past Dream Lake to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. From the lake, follow the climbers' trail above and around its south shore to the foot of the north face of Hallett Peak. Englishman's Route is the big arch on the east-facing side of the north face. The upper half can also be reached from the foot of Hallett Chimney. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Same line as the rock route co_englishman_s_route in co_hallett_peak; descent from area page; upper-half access from route page. Possible duplicate across areas.

set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and take the trail to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. At the shore, look left for the climbers' trail, then climb it up and right, contouring above the lake to the base of the big rock buttresses. Continue along the cliff base, then turn right and work up the gorge, staying slightly left of its middle to the obvious base of the couloir. The approach to the end of Tyndall Gorge is long. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree on the trail; summit is a short walk from the top but no descent is stated, so omitted.
